blocks.html: Physical Servers
blocks.text: Physical Servers

blocks.html: A real, tangible machine dedicated entirely to running your server software. You own or lease it and control both hardware and software.
blocks.text: A real, tangible machine dedicated entirely to running your server software. You own or lease it and control both hardware and software.

blocks.html: Used by banks and other high-security service providers primarily for regulatory compliance and data protection. In many cases, sensitive information—such as financial records—is legally required to stay within specific geographical or physical boundaries. Storing such data on servers located in another country is often prohibited. On-premises infrastructure ensures complete control over where the data resides and who can physically access it, reducing the risk of unauthorized entry or tampering that could compromise security.

rows.html: Scenario
Physical Server
Virtual Server
Containerized Server
Serverless
Bank storing sensitive customer data
Perfect fit — maximum control, meets compliance, secure on-premises.
Not ideal — data may reside in shared cloud hardware, risky for compliance.
Not ideal — containers usually run on shared infra, lower compliance control.
Not suitable — serverless is cloud-based, no physical control.
Small business launching a website
Not ideal — expensive upfront, overkill for low traffic.
Perfect fit — cheap to start, easy to scale as traffic grows.
Possible — but may be extra complexity for a simple site.
Not suitable — site needs to be always online, serverless not good for persistent hosting.
SaaS app with microservices (payments, users, analytics)
Not ideal — too slow to scale and inefficient for many small services.
Works — but will consume more resources than needed for many services.
Perfect fit — isolates services, fast deployment, efficient resource usage.
Not suitable — long-running services don’t fit event-driven model.
Image processing after file upload
Not ideal — keeping a physical server idle for rare events wastes money.
Not ideal — same idle cost problem as physical.
Possible — containers can run batch jobs, but still billed while running.
Perfect fit — runs only when triggered, no cost when idle.
Large e-commerce site with seasonal spikes
Works — but scaling is slow and costly (buying hardware).
Good fit — can scale virtual machines up/down with demand.
Good fit — can scale microservices independently during peak times.
Not ideal — constant baseline traffic makes serverless costs high.
